industry: Communication Equipment / Network Test and Measurement
thesis: Viavi is the pure-play test-and-measurement toll booth on optical networking: every 400G, 800G and 1.6T transceiver, switch and AI fabric has to be validated, and Viavi sells the lab, production and field instruments that do it. FY2026 revenue grew 40% to $1.518B with non-GAAP operating margin up 630bps to 20.6% and non-GAAP EPS doubling to $1.00, as the data center ecosystem grew to roughly 50% of the NSE segment and the $425M Spirent high-speed-Ethernet acquisition closed and integrated ahead of plan. At ~25x guided forward non-GAAP EPS with a roughly net-cash balance sheet, the setup is attractive, but the stock is up 226% in a year and the growth is now levered to hyperscaler optical capex — a cycle Viavi does not control.

financials.cash: $656.7M cash, short-term investments and restricted cash (vs $650M principal debt)
financials.segments: Network and Service Enablement $1,182.9M (+52.3%); Optical Security and Performance Products $335.4M (+9.0%)

drivers: 1.6T Ethernet reaches volume parity with 800G during calendar 2027 while the 800G installed base keeps upgrading, extending the test cycle rather than ending it
Co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching broaden beyond the initial hyperscaler; both are more complex to build, so test intensity per port rises
Quarterly revenue crosses $500M during calendar 2027 (management now expects this earlier than the original fiscal-2028 target)
Operating leverage carries non-GAAP operating margin to the mid-to-high 20s as NSE lab and production mix (high-70s gross margin) outgrows field instruments
Aerospace and defense — ~17% of NSE and now CMMC Level 2 certified across radio test, avionics, synthetic/modular and PNT lines — compounds on PNT resilience and allied defense budgets
Spirent synergies plus the seasonally stronger December quarter lift FY2027 non-GAAP EPS toward $2.00, supporting a re-rating to the $70 top-of-street target

assumptions: FY2027 revenue of roughly $1.85–1.95B (Q1 guided to $450–460M) as data center and A&D growth offsets a service provider base growing only 1–2%
Non-GAAP operating margin holds in the 24–27% range; Q1 FY2027 is guided to 27.1% but includes a one-off $11M tariff refund worth ~100bps
FY2027 non-GAAP EPS of approximately $1.65–1.80 (consensus, not company-guided beyond the $0.40–0.42 Q1 range)
Multiple holds near 28–30x forward non-GAAP EPS, in line with the current 9-analyst consensus target of ~$55
GAAP results stay near breakeven as acquisition amortization (~$68M/yr) and contingent-consideration remeasurement continue to absorb operating income

risks: Hyperscaler optical capex digests; data center is now ~50% of NSE, so a pause hits the fastest-growing half of the business directly
1.6T adoption is partly substitution for 800G rather than incremental, tempering the blended growth rate management has guided to
Service provider and wireless remain the drag — wireless demand is described as anemic and the base carrier business grows only 1–2%
Multiple compression: the shares carry a 1.23 beta and a $12.23–$60.43 52-week range, and already fell ~32% from the high once this year
GAAP loss-making ($0.13 loss per share in FY2026) makes the story dependent on non-GAAP adjustments that exclude $208M of FY2026 charges
$650M principal debt and $47.4M FY2026 interest expense limit buyback capacity — no shares were repurchased in Q4 FY2026
Tariffs, semiconductor cost inflation and China exposure (Asia-Pacific is 30.9% of revenue) pressure gross margin and supply

catalysts.event: Q1 FY2027 results — guided to $450–460M revenue, non-GAAP EPS $0.40–0.42 and 27.1% operating margin; watch whether data center holds above 50% of NSE
Co-packaged optics revenue acceleration and Spirent's seasonally strongest quarter (55% of Spirent revenue falls in the second half of the calendar year)
Q2 FY2027 results — first read on whether the $500M quarterly revenue milestone is reachable within calendar 2027
1.6T Ethernet expected to reach volume parity with 800G, the single largest swing factor for NSE growth
Optical circuit switching adoption broadening beyond the initial hyperscaler customer
Extension of CMMC Level 2 certification to the Inertial Labs PNT product lines acquired in 2025, widening eligibility for US defense contracts

key_risks: Concentration in hyperscaler AI/optical capex — data center is roughly half of the NSE segment
1.6T partly substitutes 800G rather than adding to it, which could temper the data center growth rate
Service provider and wireless product lines are stagnant (1–2% growth; wireless demand described as anemic)
GAAP net loss driven by ~$68M annual acquisition amortization and contingent-consideration fair-value swings ($33M in FY2026)
Valuation and momentum risk after a 226% one-year move, with a 52-week range of $12.23–$60.43
$650M principal debt ($250M 0.625% converts, $400M 3.75% notes) and $47.4M FY2026 interest expense
Tariff and semiconductor cost inflation; Asia-Pacific is 30.9% of revenue, exposing the company to China trade measures
OSP segment (anti-counterfeiting pigments, 3D sensing) grows only high-single-digits and is tied to banknote and consumer electronics cycles
Integration and execution risk on serial M&A (Spirent, Inertial Labs) after a period of heavy restructuring charges
